In [[mathematics]], the '''[[classifying space]]''' <math>\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math> '''for the [[special orthogonal group]]''' <math>\operatorname{SO}(n)</math> is the base space of the [[Universal bundle|universal]] <math>\operatorname{SO}(n)</math> [[principal bundle]] <math>\operatorname{ESO}(n)\rightarrow\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math>. This means that <math>\operatorname{SO}(n)</math> principal bundles over a [[CW complex]] up to isomorphism are in bijection with [[homotopy]] classes of its [[Continuous function|continuous]] maps into <math>\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math>. The isomorphism is given by [[Pullback bundle|pullback]]. A particular application are [[Principal SO(2)-bundle|principal SO(2)-bundles]].

== Definition ==
There is a canonical inclusion of real oriented Grassmannians given by <math>\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{R}^k)\hookrightarrow\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{R}^{k+1}),
V\mapsto V\times\{0\}</math>. Its colimit is:<ref>Milnor & Stasheff 74, section 12.2 The Oriented Universal Bundle on page 151</ref>

: <math>\operatorname{BSO}(n)
:=\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{R}^\infty)
:=\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{R}^k).</math>

Since real oriented Grassmannians can be expressed as a [[homogeneous space]] by:

: <math>\widetilde\operatorname{Gr}_n(\mathbb{R}^k)
=\operatorname{SO}(n+k)/(\operatorname{SO}(n)\times\operatorname{SO}(k))</math>

the group structure carries over to <math>\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math>.

== Simplest classifying spaces ==

* Since <math>\operatorname{SO}(1)
\cong 1</math> is the [[trivial group]], <math>\operatorname{BSO}(1)
\cong\{*\}</math> is the trivial topological space.

* Since <math>\operatorname{SO}(2)
\cong\operatorname{U}(1)</math>, one has <math>\operatorname{BSO}(2)
\cong\operatorname{BU}(1)
\cong\mathbb{C}P^\infty</math>.

== Classification of principal bundles ==
Given a [[topological space]] <math>X</math> the set of <math>\operatorname{SO}(n)</math> principal bundles on it up to isomorphism is denoted <math>\operatorname{Prin}_{\operatorname{SO}(n)}(X)</math>. If <math>X</math> is a [[CW complex]], then the map:<ref name=":36">{{cite web |access-date=2024-03-14 |language=en |title=universal principal bundle |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/universal+principal+bundle |website=[[nLab]]}}<!-- auto-translated from German by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

: <math>[X,\operatorname{BSO}(n)]\rightarrow\operatorname{Prin}_{\operatorname{SO}(n)}(X),
[f]\mapsto f^*\operatorname{ESO}(n)</math>

is [[Bijection|bijective]].

== Cohomology ring ==
The [[cohomology ring]] of <math>\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math> with coefficients in the [[Field (mathematics)|field]] <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math> of [[GF(2)|two elements]] is generated by the [[Stiefel–Whitney class|Stiefel–Whitney classes]]:<ref name=":9">Milnor & Stasheff, Theorem 12.4.</ref><ref>Lawson & Michelson 90, Theorem B.8</ref><ref name=":34">Hatcher 02, Example 4D.6.</ref>

: <math>H^*(\operatorname{BSO}(n);\mathbb{Z}_2)
=\mathbb{Z}_2[w_2,\ldots,w_n].</math>

The results holds more generally for every ring with [[Characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]] <math>\operatorname{char}=2</math>.

The cohomology ring of <math>\operatorname{BSO}(n)</math> with coefficients in the field <math>\mathbb{Q}</math> of [[Rational number|rational numbers]] is generated by [[Pontryagin class|Pontrjagin classes]] and [[Euler class]]:<ref>Lawson & Michelson 90, Theorem B.14</ref>

: <math>H^*(\operatorname{BSO}(2n);\mathbb{Q})
\cong\mathbb{Q}[p_1,\ldots,p_n,e]/(p_n-e^2),</math>
: <math>H^*(\operatorname{BSO}(2n+1);\mathbb{Q})
\cong\mathbb{Q}[p_1,\ldots,p_n].</math>

== Infinite classifying space ==
The canonical inclusions <math>\operatorname{SO}(n)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{SO}(n+1)</math> induce canonical inclusions <math>\operatorname{BSO}(n)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{BSO}(n+1)</math> on their respective classifying spaces. Their respective colimits are denoted as:

: <math>\operatorname{SO}
:=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\operatorname{SO}(n);</math>
: <math>\operatorname{BSO}
:=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\operatorname{BSO}(n).</math>

<math>\operatorname{BSO}</math> is indeed the classifying space of <math>\operatorname{SO}</math>.
